correctness.rationale: Tridiagonal determinant recurrence yields J^N(U_N(lambda/2J)+i g U_{N-1}(lambda/2J)). Every eigenvalue has strictly negative imaginary part by terminal nonzero eigenvector component. Substitution lambda=-2iJ sinh u yields g=cosh((N+1)u)/sinh(Nu) for even N, and g=sinh((N+1)u)/cosh(Nu) for odd N. The even log has strictly positive second derivative and one minimum; the odd function is strictly increasing. Nonvanishing second derivative at the minimum implies algebraic multiplicity exactly two; irreducible tridiagonal eigenspace dimension one implies a defective second-order EP. Pointwise monotonicity in real N and exponential q_N=e^(-2Nu_N) imply q_N~1/(4N) and the stated logarithmic threshold correction. Independent finite matrix/Chebyshev eigenchecks returned g2=2,g4=1.55302604,g6=1.39202881,g100=1.03542380. The claims are only on the negative imaginary axis; no global off-axis collision assertion.

final_claim: A uniform N-site nearest-neighbor chain with one terminal Markovian loss -i kappa/2 has exactly one simple negative-imaginary eigenvalue for odd N, and 0, one defective double, or two such locations for even N according to g=kappa/(2J) relative to g_N=min cosh((N+1)u)/sinh(Nu). The even-length thresholds decrease to 1 as 1+[log(4N)+1+o(1)]/(2N).
